# pw-foundation

> The dependency-light foundation for a Python project: structured logging, an exception hierarchy that separates expected domain failures from real errors, configuration resolved from the environment, console output and parallel helpers, a `Service` base class, pure utilities, and a structural build gate (`pw-guards`) that fails CI on file-size, layering and opt-in function-length, comment-budget and framework-check violations. Five dependencies (python-dotenv, pyyaml, structlog, nanoid, rich), no extras. pw-core — the LLM, database and web framework — depends on it.

Published to PyPI as `pw-foundation` (Python 3.12+); pin `pw-foundation~=1.0` (two components — the 1.x line is additive-only). Docs ship inside the package under `pw_foundation/docs/`, so an installed copy always matches its version — in a consumer repo, `pw-setup` links them at `docs/pw-foundation/`. The URLs below render `main`, the development line.

## Start here

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phierceweb/pw-foundation/main/README.md): overview, install, what you get
- [INSTALLATION](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phierceweb/pw-foundation/main/src/pw_foundation/docs/INSTALLATION.md): pinning, editable installs alongside pw-core, verification
- [Module index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phierceweb/pw-foundation/main/src/pw_foundation/docs/modules.md): one line per module, grouped by concern
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phierceweb/pw-foundation/main/CHANGELOG.md): release history
- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phierceweb/pw-foundation/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
